translations.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
He was in the beginning with God.
All things were made through him, and without him not one thing was made of all that was made.
With him was life, and that life was the light of men.
And the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not overtake it.
There was a man sent from God, and his name was John.
He came as a witness, to bear witness to the light, so that all might believe through him.
He himself was not the light, but came so that he might bear witness concerning the light.
There was the true light, which gives light to every person coming into the world.
He was in the world, and the world was made through him, and the world did not know him.
He came to his own, and his own did not receive him.
But as many as received him, to them he gave the power to become children of God, those who believe in his name,
who were born not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of a man, but of God.
And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we beheld his glory, glory as of the only-begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth.
John bore witness concerning him, cried out and said: This is the one of whom I said: He who comes after me was before me, for he is prior to me.
For from his fullness we have all received grace upon grace.
For the law was given through Moses, but grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.
No one has ever seen God; but the only-begotten Son, who was in the bosom of the Father, he has made him known.
And this is the testimony of John, when the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to him, to ask him: Who are you?
And he confessed and did not deny; he confessed: I am not the Christ.
And they asked him: Who then are you? Are you Elijah? And he said: I am not. Are you the prophet? And he answered: No.
And they said to him: Tell us who you are, so that we may bring back word to those who sent us. What do you say about yourself?
And he said: I am the voice of one crying out in the wilderness: Make straight the ways of the Lord, as the prophet Isaiah said.
And those who had been sent were from among the Pharisees.
They asked him and said to him: Why then do you baptize, if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the prophet?
John said to them: I baptize you with water, but among you stands one whom you do not know,
who is to come after me, the straps of whose sandals I am not worthy to untie.
This took place in Bethabara, beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing.
On the next day he saw Jesus coming to him, and he said: Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sins of the world.
This is the one of whom I said: After me comes a man who was before me, for he is greater than I.
I did not know him, but so that he might be revealed to Israel, for this reason I came baptizing with water.
John bore witness and said: I saw the Spirit of God, like a dove, descending from heaven, and it remained upon him.

I did not know him, but the one who sent me to baptize with water, he said to me: The one upon whom you see the Spirit descending and remaining upon him, he is the one who will baptize with the Holy Spirit.
And I have seen and borne witness that this is the Son of God.
On the next day John was standing again, and two of his disciples.
And he looked at Jesus as he was walking, and said: Behold, Christ, the Lamb of God.
And the two disciples heard him say this, and they followed Jesus.
Jesus turned and saw them following him, and he said to them: What are you looking for? And they said to him: Rabbi (which is translated Teacher), where are you staying?
He said to them: Come and see. And they went and saw where he was staying, and they remained with him that day; and it was about the tenth hour.
Andrew too, the brother of Simon Peter, was one of the two who heard from John and followed him.
He first found his brother Simon and said to him: We have found the Messiah, which in translation is Christ.
He brought him to Jesus. Jesus looked at him and said: You are Simon, son of Jonah; you shall be called Cephas, which is translated Rock.
On the next day he wanted to go out to Galilee, and he found Philip, and Jesus said to him: Follow me.
Now Philip was from Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter.
Philip found Nathanael and said to him: We have found the one of whom Moses wrote in the Law and the Prophets: Jesus, son of Joseph, from Nazareth.
Nathanael said to him: Can anything good come from Nazareth? Philip said to him: Come and see.
When Jesus saw Nathanael coming toward him, he said: Behold, truly an Israelite, in whom there is no deceit.
Nathanael said to him: How do you know me? Jesus answered and said to him: Before Philip called you, when you were under the fig tree, I saw you.
Nathanael answered him and said: Rabbi, you are the Son of God, you are the King of Israel.
Jesus answered and said to him: Because I told you that I saw you under the fig tree, you believe. You shall see greater things than this.
And he said to them: Amen, amen, I say to you: you shall see the heavens opened and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man.
And on the third day there was a wedding at Cana of Galilee, and the mother of Jesus was there.
Jesus and his disciples were invited to that wedding.
And when the wine ran short, his mother said to Jesus: "They have no wine."
Jesus said to her: "What is there between me and you, woman? My hour has not yet come."
His mother said to the servants: Whatever he tells you, do it.
Six stone water jars were standing there, in keeping with the manner of purification of the Jews, into which they would pour two or three measures each.
And Jesus said to them: Fill those jars with water! And they filled them to the brim.
And he said to them: Now draw some out and take it to the master of the feast! And they took it to him.

And when the master of the feast tasted the water that had become wine, and did not know where it came from (though the servants who had filled the jars with water knew), the master of the feast called the bridegroom
and said: Every man sets out the good wine first and, when they have become drunk, then the worse. But you have kept the good wine until now.
Jesus did this, the first of his signs, at Cana of Galilee, and revealed his glory, and his disciples believed in him.
After this Jesus went down to Capernaum, he and his mother and his brothers and his disciples with him, and he stayed there not many days.
And the Passover of the Jews was near, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
And he found in the temple those selling oxen and sheep and doves, and the money-changers sitting.
And he made a whip out of ropes and drove all of them out of the temple, the oxen and the sheep; and he poured out the coins of the money-changers and overturned their tables.
And to the dove-sellers he said: "Take these things away from here, and do not make my Father's house a house of trade."
And his disciples remembered, for it is written: The zeal for your house has consumed me.
The Jews answered and said to him: What sign do you show us, since you do this?
Jesus answered and said to them: Destroy this temple, and on the third day I will raise it up.
The Jews said to him: This temple was built in forty-six years, and will you raise it up in three days?
But he was speaking of the temple of his body.
And when he rose from the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this, and they believed the scripture and the word that Jesus had spoken to them.
And when he was in Jerusalem at the feast of Passover, many believed in his name, for they saw the signs that he was doing.
But Jesus himself did not entrust himself to them, because he knew them all.
And because he had no need that anyone should testify about man, for he himself knew what was in man.
There was a certain man of the Pharisees, Nicodemus by name, a ruler of the Jews.
This man came to Jesus by night and said to him: Rabbi, I know that you have come from God as a teacher, for no one is able to do these signs that you do unless God were with him.
Jesus answered and said to him: Amen, amen I say to you: unless someone is born a second time, he cannot see the kingdom of God.
Nicodemus said to him: How can an old man be born? Surely it is not possible to enter his mother's womb a second time and be born?
Jesus answered and said to him: "Amen, amen, I say to you: unless someone is born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God.
What is born of the flesh is flesh, and what is born of the Spirit is spirit.
Do not be amazed at this, that I said to you: You must be born a second time.
For the spirit blows wherever it wishes, and you hear its voice, but you do not know where it comes from or where it goes. So it is with everyone born of the Spirit.
Nicodemus answered and said: How can this be?
Jesus said to him: You are the teacher of Israel, and do you not know this?
Amen, amen I say to you: what we know we speak, and what we have seen we testify, and you do not accept our testimony.
If I have told you earthly things and you do not believe, how then will you believe if I tell you heavenly things?
And no one has ascended to heaven except the one who descended from heaven, the Son of Man.
And just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up,
so that whoever believes in him may have eternal life.
For God so loved the world that he gave it even his only-begotten Son, so that everyone who believes in him may not perish but may have eternal life.
For God did not send his Son into the world to judge the world, but so that the world might be saved through him.
Whoever believes in him will not be judged, but whoever does not believe is already judged, because he has not believed in the name of the Son of God.
And this is the judgment: that the light was sent into the world, and people loved the darkness rather than the light, for their deeds were evil.
For everyone who does evil hates the light and does not come to the light, so that his deeds may not be exposed.
But whoever does what is true comes to the light, so that his deeds may be made manifest, because they have been done through God.
After this Jesus and his disciples came into the land of Judea, and he stayed there with them and baptized.
John too was baptizing at Aenon, near Salim, for there was much water there, and many came and were baptized.
For John had not yet been thrown into prison.
And there was an inquiry by the disciples of John with the Jews concerning purification.
They came to John and said to him: "Rabbi, the one who was with you beyond the Jordan, the one you testified about, behold, he is baptizing, and everyone is going to him."
John answered and said to them: "A man cannot take anything at all by himself unless it has been given to him from heaven."
You yourselves testify for me that I said: 'I am not the Christ, but I have been sent before him.'
He who has the bride is the bridegroom; but the friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices with joy at the voice of the bridegroom. This joy of mine has been fulfilled.
He must increase and I must decrease.
He who comes from above is over all. And he who is from the earth is of the earth and speaks of what is of the earth, but he who comes from heaven,
what he has seen and heard, to this he testifies, and no one accepts his testimony.
Whoever has accepted his testimony has set his seal to this: that God is true.
For he whom God has sent speaks the words of God, for God does not give the Spirit by measure.
The Father loves the Son and has given everything into his hands.
Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life, but whoever disobeys the Son will not see life; rather, the wrath of God remains upon him.
When the Lord perceived that the Pharisees had heard that Jesus had more disciples and was baptizing more than John,
and yet Jesus himself did not baptize, but his disciples did,
he left Judea and went away to Galilee.
he had to pass through Samaria.
And he came to a city of Samaria called Sychar, near the estate that Jacob gave to his son Joseph.
And Jacob's spring was there, and Jesus, tired from walking on the road, sat down by the spring. And it was about the sixth hour.
A woman came from Samaria to draw water. Jesus said to her: "Give me water to drink."
For his disciples had gone away into the city to buy food.
The Samaritan woman said to him: "How is it that you, being a Jew, ask for water from me, a Samaritan woman?" For Jews do not associate with Samaritans.

Jesus answered and said to her: "If you had known the gift of God, and who it is who says to you, 'Give me water, that I may drink,' you would have asked him, and he would have given you living water."
The woman said: "Lord, you have no vessel for drawing, and this well is deep. From where do you have living water?
Are you perhaps greater than our father Jacob, who gave us this well? And he himself drank from it, and his sons and his flock."
Jesus answered and said to her: "Everyone who drinks of this water will thirst again.
But whoever drinks of the water that I will give him will no longer thirst forever; rather, the water that I will give him will become in him a spring of water going to eternal life."
The woman said to him: "Lord, give me that water, so that I may no longer thirst and may not come here to draw."
Jesus said to her: "Go and call your husband and come here,"
The woman answered and said to him: I have no husband. Jesus said to her: You have said well that you have no husband,
for you have had five husbands, and the one you have now is not your husband; what you have said is true.
The woman said to him: "Lord, I see that you are a prophet.
Our fathers worshiped on this mountain, and you say that Jerusalem is the place where it is right to worship.
Jesus said to her: Woman, believe me, for the hour is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem.
You worship what you do not know; but we worship what we know, for salvation is from the Jews.
But the hour is coming, and is already here, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and in truth, for the Father seeks such people as his worshipers.
God is spirit, and it is right for his worshipers to worship in spirit and in truth.
The woman said to him: I know, Lord, that the Messiah is coming, who is called Christ; when he comes, he will tell us everything.
Jesus said to her: "I am he, who is speaking to you."
And just at this word his disciples came, and they were amazed that he was speaking with a woman. Yet no one said to him: What are you seeking? or: What are you saying with her?
And the woman left her water jar and went away to the city and told the people everything:
Come and see a man who told me everything that I have done. Could this be the Christ?
And they came out of the city and came to him.
And just at this word the disciples were speaking to him and said to him: Rabbi, eat!
But he said to them: I have food to eat that you do not know about.
The disciples said to one another: Has someone brought him food?
Jesus said to them: This is my food: that I do the will of him who sent me and accomplish his work.
Do you not say: There are yet four months, and the harvest comes? Behold, I tell you: lift up your eyes and see the fields, for they are already white for harvest.
And the reaper will receive a wage and gather fruit for eternal life, so that the sower and the reaper may rejoice together with him.
For in this the saying is true, that one is the one who sowed and another is the reaper.
I send you to reap that for which you did not labor. Others have labored, and you have entered into their labor."
And many from that city, of the Samaritans, believed in him through the word of the woman, for she testified: He told me everything that I have done.
And when the Samaritans came, they asked him to stay with them. And he stayed there with them two days.
And a much greater number believed because of his words.
And they said to the woman: We no longer believe because of your word, for we ourselves have heard from him, and we know that this is truly the Savior of the world.
And after those two days he went out from there to Galilee.
For Jesus himself testified that a prophet has no honour in his own country.
And when he came to Galilee, the Galileans received him, for they had seen everything that he had done in Jerusalem at the feast, for they too had come to the feast.
Jesus came again to Cana of Galilee, where he had made the water into wine. And there was a certain royal official who had come, whose son was sick in Capernaum.
This man heard that Jesus had come from Judea to Galilee; he came to him and begged him to go and heal his son, who was close to death.
Jesus said to him: Unless you see miracles and signs, you will not believe.
The royal official said to him, "Lord, come before the child dies."
Jesus said to him, "Go; your son lives." And the man believed the word that Jesus spoke to him, and he went away.
And as he was going on his way, his servants came to meet him, and they told him, saying: Your son is alive.
He asked them: At what hour did he get better? They said to him: Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him.
And the boy's father remembered that it was at that very hour that Jesus had said to him: Your son is alive. And he believed, and all his household.
This again was the second miracle that Jesus performed, when he came from Judea to Galilee.
After this there was a feast of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
And there is in Jerusalem, at the Sheep Pool, a pond which is called in Hebrew Bethesda; it had five porticoes.
And in it lay a multitude of the sick, blind, lame and withered, who were waiting for the stirring of the water.
For an angel would come down to the pool year by year and stir the water; and whoever went down first at the troubling of the water would be healed of all infirmities.
There was a certain man there who had spent thirty-eight years in sickness.
Jesus saw this man lying there and perceived that he had been in his sickness for many years, and he said to him: Do you wish to be healed?
The sick man answered: Lord, I have no one to throw me into this pool when this water is troubled. While I am making my way there, another goes down before me and is healed.
Jesus said to him: "Get up, pick up your bed and walk!"
And the man was made well, and he took up his bed and went away. Now that day was the Sabbath.
The Jews said to him: It is the Sabbath, and it is not lawful for you to take up your bed.
But he answered and said to them: The one who healed me said to me: Take up your bed and walk.
Those Jews questioned him and said: Who is it who said to you: Take up your bed and walk?
But the man who had been healed did not know who it was, for Jesus had slipped away, since there was a crowd in that place.
After this Jesus found him in the temple and said to him: Behold, you have been made well; sin no more, so that nothing worse may happen to you.
The man went away and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had healed him.
And because of this those Jews persecuted Jesus, because he was doing this on the Sabbath.
But Jesus answered and said to them: My Father is working until now, and I too am working.
Because of this those Jews sought all the more to kill Jesus, because not only was he breaking the Sabbath, but he was also calling God his own Father and making himself equal to God.

Jesus answered and said to them: Amen, amen, I say to you: the Son of Man is not able to do anything at all by himself, unless he sees the Father doing some work; for whatever the Father does, the Son likewise does in the same way.
For the Father loves the Son and shows him everything that he does, and he will show him works greater than this, so that you may marvel.
For just as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, so also the Son gives life to whomever he wishes.
Nor does the Father judge anyone, but he has given all judgment to the Son,
so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father; for whoever honors the Son honors the Father who sent him.
Amen, amen, I say to you that whoever hears my words and believes the one who sent me has eternal life, and he will not enter into judgment, but will pass from death to life.
Amen, amen, I say to you: the hour is coming, and is already here, when the dead will hear the words of the Son of God; and those who hear will live.
For just as the Father has life in himself, so also he has given to the Son to have life in himself.
And he has given him authority to execute judgment as well, because he is the Son of Man.
Do not marvel at this, for the hour is coming in which all who are in the tombs will hear his voice.
And they will come out: those who have done good will rise to eternal life, but those who have done evil to the resurrection of judgment.
I am not able to do anything of myself, but as I hear, I judge, and my judgment is just, for I do not seek my own will, but the will of the one who sent me.
If I bear witness about myself, my testimony is not true.
There is another who testifies about me, and I know that the testimony he gives about me is true.
You sent to John, and he bore true witness.
But I do not accept testimony from man; rather, I say these things so that you may be saved.
For he was a burning and shining lamp, and you were willing for a time to rejoice in his light.
But I have testimony greater than John's, for the work that the Father has given me to accomplish, these same works testify concerning me, that the Father has sent me.
And the Father who sent me, he has testified concerning me. You have neither ever heard his voice nor seen his form.
And his word does not abide in you, for the one whom he sent, him you do not believe.
Search the Scriptures, for you think within yourselves that you have eternal life; and they are the ones that testify concerning me.
And you do not want to come to me, so that you may have life.
I do not receive glory from men.
But I know you, that you do not have the love of God within yourselves.
I have come in the name of my Father, and you did not receive me; if another comes in his own name, him you will receive.
How then can you believe, when you receive glory from one another and do not seek the glory of the only God?
Do not think that I will accuse you before the Father. There is one who accuses you: Moses, in whom you have set your hope.
If you had believed Moses, you would have believed me also, for he wrote concerning me.
If you do not believe his writings, how will you believe my words?
After this Jesus crossed over to the other side of the Sea of Galilee, that is, of Tiberias.
And a great crowd followed him, because they saw the signs that he was doing upon the sick.
And Jesus went up on a mountain and sat down there with his disciples.
And the Passover, the feast of the Jews, was near.
Jesus lifted up his eyes and saw that a great crowd was coming to him. He said to Philip, "Where shall we buy bread, so that these may eat?"
But he said this to test him, for he himself knew what he was going to do.
Philip said to him, "Two hundred drachmas' worth of bread is not enough for them, for each one to receive even a little."
One of his disciples, Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, said to him,
There is a boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish, but what is this before so many?
Jesus said to them: Make these men sit down. There was much grass in that place, and the men sat down, in number about five thousand.
And Jesus took the loaves and gave thanks and gave them to those who were seated; likewise also of the fish, as much as they wanted.
And when they were filled, he said to his disciples, "Gather up the leftover fragments, so that nothing may be lost."
And they gathered and filled twelve baskets with the fragments of the five barley loaves, which were left over by those who had eaten.
And when those men saw the sign that he had done, they said: This is truly the prophet who has come into the world.
But Jesus perceived that they were coming to seize him in order to make him king, and he withdrew and went away to the mountain, he himself alone.
And when evening came, his disciples went down to the sea
and got into the boat and were going across the sea to Capernaum. And it had just grown dark, and Jesus had not yet come to them.
And the sea was being stirred up by a great wind.
And when they had just gone about twenty-five or thirty stadia, they saw Jesus walking on the sea, and he was near the boat. And they were afraid.
But he said to them, "It is I; do not be afraid!"
And they wanted to take him into the boat. And immediately the boat was found at the land to which they were going.

On the next day the crowd that was standing across the sea knew that there was no other boat there except only the one that the disciples of Jesus had entered, and that Jesus had not entered that boat with the disciples, but only his disciples had entered.
Other boats also came from Tiberias, near the place where they had eaten the bread that the Lord blessed, and he gave thanks.
When the crowd saw that Jesus was not there, nor his disciples, they brought up boats and came to Capernaum, and they were seeking Jesus.
And they found him on the other side of the sea and said to him, "Rabbi, when did you come here?"
Jesus answered and said to them: Amen, amen I say to you: you seek me, not in order to see signs, but because you ate of the loaves and were filled.
Do not work for food that perishes, but for food that endures to eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you, for on him the Father, God, has set his seal.
They said to them: What shall we do, that we may work the work of God?
Jesus answered and said to them, "This is the work of God: that you believe in him whom he has sent."
And they said to him: What sign do you do, that we may see and believe you? What do you do?
Our fathers ate manna in the wilderness, as it is written: 'He gave them bread from heaven to eat.'"
Jesus said to them: Amen, amen I say to you: it was not Moses who gave you bread from heaven, but my Father gave you the true bread from heaven.
For the bread of God is that which came down from heaven and gave life to the world.
They said to him: Lord, give us this bread always.
Jesus said to them: I am the bread of life; whoever comes to me will not hunger, and whoever believes in me will never thirst.
But I told you: you have seen me and you do not believe.
All that my Father gives me will come to me; and whoever comes to me I will not drive out.
For I have come down from heaven, not to do my own will, but the will of him who sent me.
For this is the will of my Father who sent me: that of all that he gives me I should not lose any of them, but should raise him up on the last day.
For this is the will of my Father: that whoever sees the Son and believes in him should have eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day.
The Jews murmured about him because he said: I am the bread that came down from heaven.
And they said: Is this not Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father we know? How then does he now say: I came down from heaven?
Jesus answered and said to them: Do not murmur among one another.
No one is able to come to me unless my Father who sent me brings him to me, and I will raise him up on the last day.
It is written in the prophets: 'They shall all be taught by God.' Everyone who has heard from the Father and has learned comes to me.
Not that anyone has seen the Father, except the one who was with God; he has seen the Father.
Amen, amen, I say to you: whoever believes in me has eternal life.
I am the bread of life.
Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness and died.
This is the bread that came down from heaven, so that if anyone eats of it, he will not die.
I am the bread of life, who came down from heaven. If anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever. And the bread that I will give is my flesh, which I will give for the life of the world.
The Jews disputed among themselves and said: 'How can this man give us his flesh to eat?'
Jesus said to them: 'Amen, amen, I say to you: unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you do not have life in yourselves.'
But whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day.
For my flesh is true food, and my blood is true drink.
And whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood abides in me, and I in him.
As the living Father sent me, and I also live through the Father, so whoever eats of me, he too will live through me.
For this is the bread that came down from heaven. It is not as when your fathers ate the manna and died. But whoever eats this bread will live forever.
He said this in the synagogue as he was teaching in Capernaum.
Many of his disciples who heard this said: 'This word is harsh. Who can listen to it?'
Jesus knew in his spirit that his disciples were murmuring about this; he said to them: 'Does this cause you to stumble?'
What if you see the Son of Man ascending to where he was before?
It is the spirit that gives life, while the flesh is of no use; the words that I speak to you are spirit and life.
'But there are some of you who do not believe.' For Jesus knew from the beginning who they were who did not believe, and who it was who would betray him.
And he said to them: 'For this reason I told you that no one can come to me unless it has been given to him by my Father.'
Because of this many of his disciples turned back and no longer walked with him.
Jesus said to the Twelve: Do you also want to go away?
Simon Peter answered him and said: 'Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the word of eternal life.'
'And we have believed and have come to know that you are the Christ, the Son of the living God.'
Jesus answered and said to them: 'Did I not choose you, the Twelve? And one of you is a devil.'
Now he was speaking of Judas son of Simon, the Iscariot, for he was going to betray him, he who was one of the Twelve.
After this Jesus went about in Galilee, and he did not wish to go to Judea, because the Jews were seeking to kill him.
Now the feast of the Jews, which was that of Tabernacles, was near.
His brothers said to him: Cross over from here and go to Judea, so that your disciples too may see your works that you are doing.
For no one does anything in secret and yet wishes it to be made known. If you do these things, show yourself to the world.
For not even his brothers believed in him.
Jesus said to them: My time has not yet come, but your time is always ready.
For the world cannot hate you, but it hates me, because I testify concerning it that its works are evil.
You go up to this feast; but I am not going up to this feast, for my time has not yet been fulfilled.
He said this to them and stayed in Galilee.
And when his brothers had gone up to the feast, then Jesus himself also went up, not openly but in secret.
But the Jews were looking for him at the feast and saying: Where is he?
And there was murmuring about him among the people. Some were saying: He is good; and others were saying: No, rather he leads the people astray.
Yet no one spoke openly about him for fear of the Jews.
And when the feast was already half over, Jesus went up to the temple and began teaching.
The Jews were amazed and said: How does this man know the Scriptures without having been taught?
Jesus answered them and said: This teaching of mine is not mine, but belongs to him who sent me.
If anyone does his will, he will know about the teaching, what it is: whether it is from God, or whether I speak on my own.
He who speaks on his own seeks his own glory; but he who seeks the glory of the one who sent him is true, and there is no falsehood in him.
Or did not Moses give you the law? And yet none of you keeps his law. Why do you seek to kill me?
The people answered and said to him: You have a demon. Who is seeking to kill you?
Jesus answered and said to them: I did one work, and you are all astonished.
For this reason Moses gave you circumcision, not that it is from Moses, but from the fathers, and a man is circumcised on the Sabbath.
If a man receives circumcision on the Sabbath so that the law of Moses may not be abolished, do you blame me because I made a man entirely alive on the Sabbath?
Do not judge by appearances, but judge with right judgment.
Some of the people of Jerusalem were saying: Is this not the one whom they were seeking to kill?
And look, here he is speaking openly, and they say nothing to him. Can it be that the rulers have truly come to know that this is the Christ?
But we know where this man is from. Yet when the Christ comes, no one will know where he is from.
Jesus cried out in the temple, teaching and saying to them: You both know me and know where I am from; and I have not come on my own, but he who sent me is true, whom you do not know.
But I know him, for I am from him, and he sent me.
They sought to seize him, but no one laid hands on him, because his hour had not yet come.
And many of the people believed in him and were saying: When the Christ comes, will he perhaps do more signs than this man has done?
And the Pharisees heard the people's murmuring about him. And the chief priests and the Pharisees sent servants to arrest him.
and Jesus said: I am with you a little while longer, and then I go to the one who sent me.
You will seek me and will not find me; and where I am, you cannot come.
The Jews said to one another: Where does this man intend to go, that we will not find him? Does he perhaps intend to go to those dispersed among the Gentiles and to teach the Gentiles there?
What is this saying that he speaks: You will seek me and will not find me, and where I am, you cannot come?
And on the last day of that great feast Jesus stood, cried out and said: If anyone thirsts, let him come to me and drink.
And whoever believes in me, as the scripture has said, rivers of living water will flow from his belly.
This he said concerning the Spirit which those who believed in him were to receive, for the Holy Spirit had not yet been given, because Jesus had not yet been glorified.
Many of the people heard this word and said: This is truly the prophet;
others said: This is the Christ; and others said: Surely the Christ is not to come from Galilee?
Does not the Scripture say that the Christ shall come from the seed of David and from Bethlehem, the village where David was?
And there was a division among the people because of him.
And some of them wanted to seize him, but no one laid hands on him.
The servants of the chief priests and Pharisees came, and they said to them: Why did you not bring him?
The servants answered and said to them: Never has any man spoken as this man does.
The Pharisees answered and said to them: Have you too then been led astray?
Has any of the rulers believed in him, or any of the Pharisees?
But this people, who do not know the Law, are accursed.
Nicodemus, who had come to him earlier and was one of them, said to them:
"Does our Law condemn a man unless it first hears from him and learns what he is doing?"
They answered and said to him: "Are you also from Galilee? Search and see, for no prophet has arisen from Galilee."
And each one went to his own house.
But Jesus went up to the Mount of Olives.
And the next day he came again to the temple, and all the people were coming to him, and he was teaching them.
The chief priests and the Pharisees brought a woman and stood her in the middle
and said to him: Teacher, this woman was caught openly in adultery.
And in the Law of Moses he commands us to stone such a person. Now what do you say?
They said this to test him, so that they might have some accusation against him. But Jesus was looking downward and writing on the ground with his finger.
And as they stood a long while watching him, he then straightened up and said to them: Whoever among you is without sin, let him be the first to throw a stone at her.
And again he bent down to the ground.
And when they heard this, the elders and the scribes began, and they went out one by one, and he remained alone, and the woman stood before Jesus.
And Jesus looked at her and said to her: Woman, where are your accusers? Has no one condemned you?
And she said: No one, Lord! And Jesus said to her: Neither do I condemn you; go, and from now on sin no more.
Then Jesus spoke again and said to them: I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will not walk in darkness, but will have the light of life.
The Pharisees said to him: You bear witness about yourself, and your witness is not true.

Jesus answered and said to them: Even if I bear witness about myself, my witness is true, for I know where I have come from and where I am going; but you do not know where I came from and where I am going.
You judge according to the flesh, but I judge no one.
And if I judge, my judgment is true, for I am not alone, but it is I and the Father who sent me.
For it is also written in your law that the witness of two men is true.
I am the one who bears witness about myself, and the Father who sent me bears witness about me.
The Jews said to him: Where is your Father? Jesus answered and said to them: You know neither me nor my Father. If you knew me, you would know my Father also.
These words he spoke to them by the treasury, as he was teaching in the temple. And no one seized him, for his hour had not yet come.
Jesus said to them again: I am going away, and you will seek me, and you will perish in your sins; and where I am going, you cannot come.
The Jews said to one another: Surely he will not kill himself? For he says: Where I am going, you cannot come.
And he said to them: You are from the earth, but I am from heaven; you are of this world, but I am not of this world.
I told you that you will perish in your sins; if you do not believe that I am he, you will perish in your sins.
They said to him: Who are you? Jesus said to them: First of all, that which I am telling you.
I have many things to say and to judge concerning you, but he who sent me is true, and what I have heard from him, that I speak in the world.
But they did not understand that he was telling them about his Father.
Then Jesus said to them: When you lift up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am he, and that I do nothing of myself, but as the Father taught me, that I speak.
For he who sent me is with me; he has not left me alone, for I always do what is pleasing to him.
As he was saying this to them, many believed in him.
And Jesus said to those Jews who believed in him: If you abide in my words, you are truly my disciples.
And you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.
The Jews answered and said to him: We are descendants of Abraham and have never been slaves to anyone; how is it that you say: You will be set free?
Jesus answered and said to them: Amen, amen, I say to you that everyone who commits sin is a slave of sin.
And the slave never remains in the house forever, but the son remains forever.
If the Son sets you free, you will truly be free.
I know that you are descendants of Abraham, but you seek to kill me, because my word finds no room among you.
What I have seen from my Father, that I speak; and you, what you hear from your father, that you do.
They answered and said to him: Our father is Abraham. Jesus said to them: If you were children of Abraham, you would do the work of Abraham.
But now you seek to kill me, a man who tells you the truth, which I heard from God. Abraham did not do this.
You do the work of your father. They said to him: We were not born of fornication; we know one Father: God.
Jesus said to them: If God were your Father, you would love me, for I came forth from God and have come; for I have not come of myself, but he sent me.
Why do you not understand my words? Because you are not able to hear my words.

You are of your father the devil, and you want to do the desire of your father; for he is a murderer from the beginning, and he did not stand firm in the truth, because the truth is not with him. When he speaks a lie, he speaks from his own heart, for his father too is a liar.
But I tell you the truth, and you do not believe me.
Which of you will convict me of sin? If I tell you the truth, why do you not believe?
Whoever is from God listens to the words of God; for this reason you do not listen, because you are not from God.
The Jews answered and said to him, "Did we not say rightly that you are a Samaritan and have a demon?"
Jesus answered them and said: There is no demon with me, but I honor my Father, and you insult me.
But I do not seek my own glory; there is one who seeks it and judges.
Amen, amen, I say to you: if anyone keeps my word, he will never see death."
The Jews said to him: Now we know that you are possessed by a demon: Abraham died, and the prophets too, and you say: If anyone keeps my word, he will not see the taste of death for ever.
Are you perhaps greater than our father Abraham, who died? And the prophets perished. Whom do you make yourself out to be?
Jesus answered and said to them: If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing; but there is my Father who glorifies me, of whom you have said: He is our God.
And you do not know him, but I know him; and if I should say: I do not know him, I would be a liar like you; but I know him and I keep his words.
Abraham your father rejoiced that he would see this day of mine; and he saw it and was glad."
The Jews said to him: You are not fifty years old, and have you seen Abraham?
Jesus said to them: Amen, amen, I say to you: Before Abraham came to be, I am.
The Jews picked up stones to throw at him, but Jesus hid himself and went out of the temple, and he passed through their midst and so went away.
And as Jesus was going along, he saw a man blind from birth.
His disciples asked him, saying, "Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he was born blind?"
Jesus said to them: Neither did this man sin nor his parents, but it was so that the work of God might be revealed in him.
And I must do the work of the one who sent me while it is still day; night is coming, when no one will be able to work.
While I am in the world, I am the light of the world.
And when he had said this, he spat on the ground and made clay from the spittle, and he smeared the clay on the eyes of the blind man.
And he said to him: Go and wash in the pool of Siloam, which is translated Sent. The man went and washed, and he came back seeing.
But the neighbours, and those who had seen him before, when he was a beggar, were saying: "Is this not the man who used to sit and beg?"
Others said: This is he; but some said: No, but he is like him; but he himself said: I am he.
They asked him, "How were your eyes opened?"
But he answered and said to them: The man who is called Jesus made clay and smeared it on my eyes and said to me: Go to Siloam and wash. And I went and washed them and received my sight.
They said to him: Where is he? And he said to them: I do not know.
It was the Sabbath when he made the clay and opened his eyes.
They brought the one who had formerly been blind before the Pharisees.
Again the Pharisees asked him: How did you receive your sight? And he said to them: He put clay on my eyes, and I washed, and now I see.
Some of the Pharisees said: This man is not from God, for he does not keep the Sabbath. Others said: How can a sinful man do such a sign? And there was dispute among them.
They said to the man who had formerly been blind: "What do you say about him, since he opened your eyes?" And he said: "He is a prophet."
The Jews did not believe about him that he had been blind and had received his sight, until they called the parents of the one who had received his sight.
And they questioned them and said: "Is this your son, of whom you said that he was born blind? How then does he now see?"
His parents answered and said: "We know that this is our son and that he was born blind."
"But how he now sees, we do not know; or who opened his eyes, we do not know. Ask him; he is of age; let him speak for himself."
His parents said this because they were afraid of the Jews, for the Jews had agreed among themselves that if anyone should confess him as Christ, they would expel him from the congregation.
For this reason his parents said: "He is of age; ask him."
They called a second time the man who had formerly been blind, and said to him: "Give glory to God; we know that this man is a sinner."
He answered and said: "Whether he is a sinner, I do not know; but this one thing I know, that I was blind and now I see."
Then they said to him: "What did he do to you? How did he open your eyes?"
He answered and said to them: "I told you before, and you did not listen; why do you want to hear it again? Or do you also want to become his disciples?"
But they reviled him and said: "You are his disciple, but we are disciples of Moses."
"We know that God spoke to Moses, but as for this man, we do not know where he is from."
The man answered and said to them: "This is a marvel: you do not know where he is from, and yet he opened my eyes."
"But this I know, that God does not listen to a sinner; but if anyone is a worshipper of God and does his will, God listens to him."
Since the beginning of the world it has never been heard that anyone opened the eyes of a man born blind.
If this man were not from God, he could not do anything."
They answered and said to him: "You were born entirely in sin, and are you teaching us?" And they drove him out.
When Jesus heard that they had driven him out, he found him and said to him: "Do you believe in the Son of God?"
He answered and said: "Who is he, Lord, that I may believe in him?"
Jesus said to him: "You have seen him, and the one who is speaking with you is he."
And he said to him: "I believe, Lord," and he worshipped him.
And Jesus said: "For the judgment of this world I have come, so that those who did not see may see, and those who saw may become blind."
Some of the Pharisees who were with him heard this, and they said to him: "Are we blind too?"
Jesus said to them: "If you were blind, you would have no sin. But now you say, 'We see,' and so your sins remain.
Amen, amen, I say to you: whoever does not enter the sheepfold by the door but climbs in some other way is a thief and a robber.
"But the one who enters by the door is the shepherd of the sheep."
"To him the doorkeeper opens, and the sheep listen to his voice, and he calls his own sheep by name and leads them out."
"And when he has brought out all his own, he goes before them, and the sheep follow him, because they know his voice."
"But they do not follow a stranger; rather they flee from him, because they do not know the voice of the stranger."
Jesus told them this parable, but they did not understand what he was saying to them.
And Jesus said to them again: "Amen, amen I say to you, I am the door of the sheep."
"All who came before me were thieves and robbers, but the sheep did not listen to them,"
I am the door: if anyone enters through me, he will be saved; and he will go in and go out and find pasture.
But the thief does not come except to steal and slaughter and destroy. But I came so that they may have life and have it more abundantly.
I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd lays down his life for his sheep.
But the one appointed for hire, who is not a shepherd, whose own the sheep are not, when he sees the wolf coming, abandons the sheep and flees, and the wolf snatches them and scatters them.
For he is appointed for hire and has no concern for the sheep.
I am the good shepherd, and I know my own, and my own know me.
As the Father knows me, I also know the Father, and I lay down my life for the sheep.
And I have other sheep too, which are not of this fold; those too I must bring, and they will listen to my voice, and they will be one flock and one shepherd.
For this reason the Father loves me, because I lay down my life, so that I may take it up again.
No one takes it from me, but I lay it down of my own accord. I have authority to lay it down and I have authority to take it up again. This commandment I have received from my Father.
And again there was a division among the Jews because of this word.
And many of them were saying: "He has a demon and is raving. Why do you listen to him?"
And others said: These words are not those of one possessed by a demon. Can a demon open the eyes of a blind man?
And at that time the Feast of Dedication took place in Jerusalem; it was winter.
And Jesus was walking about in the temple, in the portico of Solomon.
The Jews surrounded him and said to him: How long will you take away our souls? If you are the Christ, tell us openly.
Jesus answered them and said to them: I told you, and you do not believe; the works which I do in the name of my Father, these testify about me.
But you do not believe, because you are not of my sheep.
My sheep listen to my voice, and I know them, and they follow me.
And I give them eternal life, and they will never perish, and no one will snatch them from my hands.
My Father, who gave them to me, is greater than all, and no one can snatch them from the hand of my Father.
I and the Father are one.
Those Jews had stones, in order to stone him.
Jesus answered them and said to them: I have shown you many good works from my Father; for which of those works are you stoning me?
The Jews said to him: We are not stoning you for a good work, but for blasphemy, because you are a man and have made yourself God.
Jesus answered them and said to them: Is it not written in the law: I said, You are gods?
If he called them gods, to whom the word of God came, and scripture cannot be annulled,
then of the one whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world, you say: He blasphemes, because I said: I am the Son of God.
If I do not do the work of my Father, do not believe me.
If I do them, even though you do not believe me, believe the works, so that you may perceive and know that the Father is with me, and I with the Father.
They sought again to seize him, and he went out from their hands.
And he crossed over beyond the Jordan, to the place where John had first been baptizing, and he stayed there.
And many came to him and said: John performed no sign; but everything that John said about this man is true.
And many believed in him there.
A certain man was sick, Lazarus of Bethany, from the village of Mary and Martha, her sister.
This was the Mary who anointed the Lord with ointment and wiped his feet with her hair, whose brother Lazarus was sick.
His sisters sent to Jesus and said to him: Lord, behold, he whom you loved is sick.
When Jesus heard this, he said: This illness is not unto death, but for the glory of God, so that the Son of God may be glorified through it.
Jesus loved Martha and her sister and Lazarus.
When Jesus heard that he was sick, he then remained two more days in the place where he was.
After this he said to his disciples: Come, let us go again to Judea.
The disciples said to him: Rabbi, just now the Jews were seeking to stone you, and are you going there again?
Jesus said to them: Are there not twelve hours of the day? If anyone walks in the day, he will not stumble, for he sees the light of this world.
And if anyone walks in the night, he stumbles, for the light is not in him.
When he had said this, after that he said to them: Lazarus, my friend, has fallen asleep, but I will go and awaken him.
The disciples said to him: Lord, if he has fallen asleep, he will recover.
But Jesus had spoken of his death, and they thought that he was speaking of the slumber of sleep.
Then Jesus said to them plainly: "Lazarus has died.
And I rejoice for your sake, so that you may believe me, that I was not there. But come, let us go to him.
Thomas, who was called the Twin, said to his fellow disciples: Come, let us go too, so that we may die with him.
And when Jesus came to Bethany, he found that he had already been four days in the tomb.
Now Bethany was near Jerusalem, only about fifteen stadia away.
And many of the Jews had come to Martha and Mary to comfort them concerning their brother.
But when Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she went to meet him, while Mary sat in the house.
Martha said to Jesus: Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.
And even now I know: whatever you ask of God, God will give you.
Jesus said to her, "Your brother will rise again."
Martha said to him: I know that he will rise in the resurrection on the last day.
Jesus said to her, "I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me, even if he dies, will live."
And everyone who lives and believes in me shall not die forever. Do you believe this?
She said to him: Yes, Lord, I have believed that you are the Christ, the Son of God, who has come into the world.
And when she had said this, she went and secretly called Mary, her sister, and said to her, "The Teacher has come and is calling you."
And when she heard this, she got up quickly and went to him.
For Jesus had not yet come into the village, but was still at the place where Martha had met him.
But those Jews who were with her in the house and were comforting them, when they saw Mary, that she rose quickly and went out, followed her, thinking that she was going to the tomb to weep for him.
But when Mary came to where Jesus was, and when she saw him, she fell at his feet and said to him: Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.
But when Jesus saw her, that she was weeping, and that those Jews who had come with her were weeping too, he shuddered in spirit, as if with anger [?]
And he said to them: Where have you laid him? They said to him: Lord, come and see.
And Jesus wept.
The Jews said: Behold, how he loved him!
Some of them said: Could not this man, who opened the eyes of the blind man, have done something so that this one also would not have died?
But Jesus again, as if with anger within himself, came to the tomb. It was a cave, and a stone lay upon it.
Jesus said to them: Take away that stone. The sister of the dead man, Martha, said to him: Lord, he already stinks, for it is the fourth day.
Jesus said to her: Did I not tell you that if you believe, you will see the glory of God?
They took away the stone. And Jesus lifted up his eyes to heaven and said: Father, I thank you, for you have heard me.
And I know that you always hear me, but I said this for the sake of this people who stand around me, so that they may believe that you sent me.
And when he had said this, he cried out with a loud voice, "Lazarus, come out!"
And the dead man came out, bound hand and foot with wrappings, and his face was covered with a cloth. Jesus said to them: Unbind him and let him go.
Many of the Jews who had come to Mary and Martha saw what he did, and they believed in him.
But some of them went away to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus had done.
And the chief priests and the Pharisees gathered an assembly and said: What are we to do, for this man performs many signs?
If we leave him alone like this, everyone will believe in him, and the Romans will come and take from us both our place and our nation,
One of them, Caiaphas, who was high priest of that year, said to them: You know nothing at all.
nor have you considered that it is better for us that one man should die for the people, and not that the whole nation should perish."
He did not say this of himself, but he was high priest of that year and spoke by prophecy, that Jesus was going to die for the nation.
And not only for the nation, but so that he might also gather together into one the scattered children of God.
From then on the Jews took counsel to kill him.
But Jesus no longer went about openly among the Jews, but went away from there to a district near the wilderness, to a city called Ephraim, and he stayed there with his disciples.
The Passover, the feast of the Jews, was near, and many went up to Jerusalem from the countryside before the Passover, which is called the Passion, in order to purify themselves.
And the Jews were looking for Jesus, and as they stood in the temple they said to one another: What do you think? Will he not come to this feast?
For the chief priests and the Pharisees had given an order that if anyone knew where he was, he should inform them, so that they might seize him.
But Jesus, six days before the Passion, came to Bethany, where Lazarus had died, whom Jesus raised from the dead.
They prepared a supper for him there, and Martha served him, and Lazarus was one of those reclining at table with him.
But Mary took a pound of ointment of genuine nard, of great price, and anointed the feet of Jesus and wiped his feet with her hair, and the whole house was filled with the fragrance of the ointment.
One of his disciples, Judas son of Simon, the Iscariot, who had it in his heart to betray him, said:
Why was this ointment not sold for three hundred drachmas and given to the poor?
But he said this, not because he had any concern for the poor, but because he was a thief and had the purse, and he carried what was put into it.
And Jesus said: Leave her alone, so that she may keep it for the day of my burial.
For the poor are always with you, but I am not always with you.
All the people of the Jews learned that Jesus was there, and they came not only for Jesus' sake, but also so that they might see Lazarus, whom he had raised from the dead.
But the chief priests took counsel to kill Lazarus as well.
For many of the Jews were coming and they believed in Jesus.
On the next day the great crowd that had come to the feast, because they heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem,
took branches of palm trees and went out to meet him, and they were crying out and saying: Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, and the King of Israel!
And Jesus found a donkey and sat on it, as it is written:
Do not be afraid, daughter of Zion! Behold, your king is coming, and he sits on the colt of a donkey.
His disciples did not understand this at first, but when Jesus was glorified, they remembered that this had been written about him, and that they had done this to him.
And the crowd that was with him bore witness to him, that he had called Lazarus from the tomb and raised him from the dead.
For this reason also the crowd was going to meet him, because they had heard that he had performed this sign.
But the Pharisees said to them: Do you see that you gain nothing? Behold, the whole world has gone after him.
There were also certain gentiles among those who had come up to worship at the feast.
These approached Philip, who was from Bethsaida of Galilee, and they were asking him and saying: Lord, we wish to see Jesus.
Philip came and told Andrew; then Andrew and Philip came and told Jesus.
And Jesus answered and said to them, "The hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.
Amen, amen, I say to you: unless a grain of wheat falls to the ground and dies, it remains alone; if it dies, it will bear much fruit.
Whoever loves his own life will lose it; and whoever hates his own life in this world will keep it for eternal life.
If anyone serves me, let him follow me; and wherever I am, there my servant will be also. And if anyone serves me, my Father will honor him.
Now my soul is troubled, and what shall I say? Father, save me from this hour. But for this reason I have come to this hour.
Father, glorify your name. A voice came to him from heaven: I have glorified you, and I will glorify you again.
But the crowd that was standing there and heard it said that it was thunder; and others said: An angel spoke to him.
Jesus answered and said to them, "This voice did not come for my sake, but for yours.
Now is the judgment of this world; now the ruler of this world will fall down below.
And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself.
But in saying this he was making known by what death he was going to die.
The crowd answered him: We have heard from the Law that the Christ will remain forever. And how do you say that the Son of Man must be lifted up?

Jesus said to them: The light is with you for only a little while longer. Walk while you have the light, so that darkness may not overtake you. Whoever walks in darkness does not know where he is going.
While you have the light, believe in the light, so that you may be sons of light. Jesus said this, and he went away and hid himself from them.
And though he had done so many signs before them, they did not believe in him.
This was so that the word of the prophet Isaiah might be fulfilled, which says: Lord, who has believed what we have heard? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?
For this reason they could not believe, because Isaiah also said:
He has blinded their eyes and hardened their hearts, so that they may not see with their eyes or understand with their hearts, and turn, and I would heal them.
Isaiah said this when he saw his glory, and he spoke about him.
Yet even among the rulers many believed in him, but because of the Pharisees they did not confess it, so that they would not be expelled from the congregation.
For they loved the glory of men more than the glory of God!
Then Jesus cried out and said: Whoever believes in me does not believe in me, but in the one who sent me.
And whoever has seen me has seen the one who sent me.
I, the light, have been sent into the world, so that everyone who believes in me may not remain in darkness.
And if anyone hears my words and does not keep them, I do not judge him, for I did not come to condemn the world, but to save the world.
But whoever despises me and does not receive my words has his own judge: the word that I have spoken, that is what will judge him on the last day.
For I have not spoken on my own, but the Father who sent me, he gave me a commandment, what I should say and what I should speak.
And I know that his commandment is eternal life. And what I say, I say just as the Father has told me.

And before the feast of Passover, that is, the Passion, Jesus knew that his hour had come, that he should depart from this world and go to the Father, for he had loved his own in this world, and he loved them completely.
And when the supper took place, the devil had entered the heart of Judas, son of Simon Iscariot, so that he would betray him.
Jesus, knowing that the Father had given everything into his hands, and that he had come from God and was going to God,
rose from the supper, laid aside his garment, took a towel, and girded himself with it.
And then he took water and poured it into the basin, and began to wash the feet of his disciples, and he wiped them with the linen cloth that he was wearing.
And he came to Simon Peter. Peter said to him: "Lord, are you going to wash my feet?"
Jesus answered and said to him: What I am doing you do not know now, but you will know afterward.
Peter said to him: You shall never wash my feet. Jesus said to him: If I do not wash your feet, you will have no part with me.
Simon Peter said to him: "Lord, not only my feet, but also my hands and my head."
Jesus said to him: One who has bathed needs nothing except to wash his feet only, for he is entirely clean. And you are clean, but not all of you.
For he knew who was betraying him. That is why he said: Not all of you are clean.
And when he had washed their feet, he then took his garment and [?], and then he said to them: Do you know what I have done to you?
You call me Teacher and Lord, and you speak rightly, for I am.
If I, the Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another's feet.
For I have given you an example: just as I have done to you, so you also should do.
Amen, amen I say to you: a servant is not greater than his lord, nor is a messenger greater than the one who sent him.
If you know this, you are blessed if you do it.
I do not say this about all of you, for I know those whom I have chosen; but it is so that the scriptures may be fulfilled: He who was eating bread with me has lifted up his heel against me.
From now on I tell you before it happens, so that when it happens you may believe that I am.
Amen, amen I say to you: if anyone receives the one whom I send, he receives me; and whoever receives me receives the one who sent me.
When Jesus had said this, he was troubled in his spirit, and he testified and said: Amen, amen I say to you that one of you will hand me over.
The disciples kept looking at one another and could not tell about whom he was speaking.
And one of his disciples was reclining against the bosom of Jesus, the one whom Jesus loved.
Simon Peter beckoned to him to ask who it was about whom he was speaking.
He leaned against the breast of Jesus and said to him: Lord, who is it?
Jesus answered and said: It is the one for whom I dip the bread and to whom I give it. And he dipped the bread and gave it to Judas Iscariot, son of Simon.
And after Judas received the bread, the devil entered into him. And Jesus said to him: What you intend to do, do quickly.
None of those sitting at table with Jesus understood why he said this to him.
For some supposed, since Judas had the money bag, that Jesus was telling him: Buy what we need for this feast, or to give something to the poor.
So he took the bread and went out immediately. And it was night.
And when Judas had gone out, Jesus said: Now the Son of Man has been glorified, and God also has been glorified in him.
And if God has been glorified in him, God will also glorify him in himself, and he will glorify him immediately.
Children, I am with you for a little while. You will seek me, and just as I said to the Jews: Where I am going, you cannot come; so now I say to you.
A new commandment I give you, that you love one another; just as I have loved you, you also should love one another.
By this all will know that you are my disciples, if you love one another.
Simon Peter said to him: Lord, where are you going? Jesus said to him: Where I am going, you cannot come now, but afterward you will follow me.
Peter said to him: “Lord, why can I not follow you? Now I will lay down my life for you.”
Jesus answered and said to him: Will you lay down your life for me? Amen, amen I say to you: the rooster will not crow until you have denied me three times.
Do not let your heart be troubled; believe in God and believe in me.
In my Father's house there are many dwelling places. If it were not so, I would have told you: I am going away to prepare a place for you.
And if I go away and prepare a place for you, I will come again and take you with me, so that where I am, there you may be also.
And where I am going, you know, and the way too you know.
Thomas said to him: "Lord, we do not know where you are going, so how can we know the way?"
Jesus said to him: I am the way and the truth and the life, and no one shall come to the Father except through me.
If you had known me, you would have known my Father also. From now on you know him, and you have seen him.
Philip said to him: "Lord, show us your Father, and that is enough for us."
Jesus said to him: For so long a time I have been with you, and do you still not know me, Philip? Whoever has seen me has seen my Father, so how can you say to me: Show us your Father?
Do you not believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in me? The words that I speak to you, I do not speak of myself, but my Father, who is in me, he does the work.
Do you believe that I am with the Father and my Father is with me? If not, then believe me because of these works.
Amen, amen, I say to you: whoever believes in me, the work that I do he too will do, and he will do greater than this, for I am going to my Father.
And whatever you ask in my name, that I will do, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
If you love me, keep my commandments.
And I will ask my Father, and he will give you another Comforter, so that he may remain with you forever,
that Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, for it does not see him, nor does it know him; but you know him, for he is with you and will be with you.
I will not leave you orphans; I will come to you.
And yet a little while, and this world will no longer see me, but you will see me, for I am alive, and you too will live.
On that day you will know that I am with my Father, and you are with me, and I am among you.
Whoever has my commandments and keeps them, he is the one who loves me. And whoever loves me will be loved by my Father, and I too will love him and will reveal myself to him.
Judas (not Iscariot) said to him: "Lord, why is it that you will reveal yourself to us and not to the world?"
Jesus answered and said to him: If anyone loves me, he will keep my words, and my Father too will love him, and we will come to him and will remain with him.
But whoever does not love me will not keep my words; and the words that you hear are not mine, but belong to the Father who sent me.
I have told you these things because I was with you.
But that Comforter, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you everything and will remind you of everything that I have said to you.
Peace I leave to you, my peace I give to you; not as the world gives do I give to you. Let your heart not be troubled, nor let it be afraid.
You have heard that I said to you: I am going away and I will come to you. If you loved me, you would rejoice that I am going to my Father, for my Father is greater than I.
And now I have told you before it happens, so that when it happens you may believe.
I will no longer speak much with you, for the ruler of this world is coming, and he will find nothing in me.
But so that the world may know that I love my Father, and as the Father commanded me, so I will do. Rise, let us go from here.
I am the true vine, and my Father is the vinedresser.
Every branch that does not bear fruit in me, he will take away; and every one that bears fruit, he will cleanse, so that it may bear more fruit.
But you are already clean through the word that I have spoken to you.
And remain in me, and I in you, for just as a vine shoot cannot bear fruit by itself unless it stays on the vine, so neither can you, unless you remain in me.
I am the vine, and you are the branches. Whoever remains in me, and I in him, this one will bear much fruit, for without me you can do nothing, not even one thing.
If anyone does not remain in me, he has been thrown outside like a vine shoot and has withered, and they will gather it and throw it into the fire, and it will burn.
If you remain with me, and my words are with you, ask whatever you wish, and it will be done for you.
By this my Father is glorified, that you bear much fruit and be my disciples.
As the Father loved me, I also have loved you; remain in my love.
If you keep my commandments, you will remain in my love, just as I have kept my Father's commandments and remain in his love.
I have said this to you so that my joy may remain in you, and that your joy may be complete.
This is my commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you.
No one has greater love than this, that he should lay down his own life for his friends.
You are my friends if you do what I command you.
I no longer call you servants, for a servant does not know what his lord is doing. But I have called you friends, for everything that I heard from my Father I have made known to you.
You did not choose me, but I chose you and appointed you, that you should go and bear fruit, and that your fruit should remain, so that whatever you ask my Father in my name, he may give you.
This I command you, that you love one another.
If the world hates you, know that it hated me first.
If you were of the world, the world would love its own; but because you are not of the world, and I chose you out of the world, for this reason the world hates you.
Remember the word that I told you: a servant is not greater than his lord. If they persecuted me, they will persecute you too; if they kept my words, they will keep yours too.
But they will do this to you on account of my name, because they do not know the one who sent me.
If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have sin; but now they have no excuse for their sins.
Whoever hates me hates my Father also.
If I had not done among them the works which no one else did, they would not have sin. But now they have both seen me and hated both me and my Father.
But this is so that the word might be fulfilled which is written in their law: "They hated me without cause."
But when the Comforter comes, whom I will send to you from my Father, the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father, he will bear witness concerning me.
And you also are witnesses, because you have been with me from the beginning.
I have told you these things so that you may not stumble.
They will put you out of the synagogue. Indeed, the hour is coming when everyone who kills you will think that he has offered a sacrifice to God.
And they will do this to you because they have not known my Father, nor me.
But I have told you these things so that, when that hour comes, you may remember them, that I told you. I did not tell you this from the beginning, because I was with you.
But now I am going to him who sent me, and does none of you ask me, "Where are you going?"
But now that I have told you this, sorrow has filled your hearts.
But I tell you the truth: it is better for you that I go away. If I do not go away, the Comforter will not come to you; if I go away, I will send him to you.
And he will come and convict the world concerning sin and righteousness and judgment:
concerning sin, thus: because they did not believe in me;
and concerning righteousness, because I am going to my Father, and you will see me no longer;
and concerning judgment, because the ruler of this world has been judged.
I still have many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now.
But when the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all truth, for he will not speak on his own, but whatever he hears he will speak, and he will tell you what is to come.
He will glorify me, for he will receive from me and tell it to you.
All that the Father has is mine; that is why I said to you, "He will receive from me and tell it to you."
A little while longer, and you will see me no longer; and again a little while, and you will see me.

His disciples said to one another: "What is this that he is telling us: 'A little while, and you will see me no longer; and again a little while longer, and you will see me'; and, 'I am going to my Father'?"
And they were saying: "What is this 'a little while'? We do not know what he is saying."

Jesus perceived that they wanted to ask him, and he said to them: "Are you inquiring among yourselves about this, that I said, 'A little while longer, and you will see me no longer; and again a little while, and you will see me'?"
Amen, amen, I say to you that you will weep and lament, but the world will rejoice; and you will grieve, but your grief will be turned into joy.

A woman, when she is giving birth, is in sorrow, because her time has come. But when she has borne the child, she no longer remembers the anguish, because of the joy that a person has been born into the world.
And you now have anguish. But I will see you again, and your hearts will rejoice, and no one will take your joy away from you.
And on that day you will ask me nothing. Amen, amen, I say to you: if you ask anything of my Father in my name, he will give it to you.
Until now you have asked for nothing. Ask and you will receive, that your joy may be full.
I have spoken these things to you in parables, but the hour is coming when I will no longer speak to you in parables, but will tell you plainly about my Father.
On that day you will ask in my name, and I do not say to you that I will ask my Father on your behalf.
For my Father himself loves you, because you have loved me and have believed that I came forth from God.
I came forth from the Father and was sent into the world, and again I am leaving the world and going to the Father.
His disciples said to him: Behold, now you are speaking openly and are not speaking any parable at all.
And now we know that you know all things and have no need for anyone to question you. By this we know that you came forth from God.
Jesus answered them and said: Do you now indeed believe?
Behold, the hour is coming and has arrived, when you will be scattered, each one to his own place, and will leave me alone; and yet I am not alone, for my Father is with me.
I have told you these things so that you may have peace in me. In this world you have tribulation, but do not be afraid, for I have overcome the world.
Jesus was saying these things, and he lifted up his eyes to heaven and said: Father, the hour has come; glorify your Son, that your Son also may glorify you.
Just as you gave him authority over all flesh, that to all whom you have given him he may give eternal life.
And this is eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you sent.
I glorified you on earth and accomplished your work, which you gave me to do.
And now glorify me, Father, with yourself, with the glory that I had in your presence before my being in this world.
I have revealed your name to the people whom you gave me out of this world; they were yours and you gave them to me, and they have kept your word.
Now they have come to know that everything you gave me, I gave to them, and that they are from you.
For the words that you gave me I have given to them, and they received them and knew truly that I came forth from you, and they believed that you sent me.
I pray for them. I do not ask for the world, but for those whom you have given me, for they are yours.
And all that is mine is yours, and what is yours is mine, and I am glorified among them.
And I am no longer in this world, but these are in the world, and I am coming to you. Holy Father, keep by your name these whom you gave me, that they may be in unity, as we are.
When I was with them, I guarded them by your name. Those whom you gave me I kept, and none of them perished except the son of perdition, that the scripture might be fulfilled.
But now I am coming to you, and I say this in the world, so that they may have my joy in full.
I gave them your words, and the world hated them, because they are not of the world, just as I am not of this world.
I do not ask that you take them out of the world, but that you keep them from evil.
They are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.
Sanctify them in truth, for your word is truth.
As you sent me into the world, I also send them into the world.
And for their sake I sanctify myself, that they too may be holy in truth.
And I do not ask for these alone, but for all who have believed in me through their word,
That all may be one, as you, Father, are in me, and I in you, that they too may be in us, that the world may believe that you sent me.
And the glory that you gave me I have given to them, that they may be one, as we are one.
I in them, and you with me, that they may be perfect in unity, and that the world may know that you sent me and loved them, as you loved me.
Father, as for these whom you gave me, I desire that where I am they too may be with me, that they may behold my glory, which you gave me, because you loved me before the creation of the world.
Righteous Father, the world did not know you, but I knew you, and these also knew that you sent me.
And I made your name known to them and will make it known, that the love with which you loved me may be among them, and I with them.
