Jesus said this and went out with his disciples across the ravine of the firs, where there was a garden, which he himself and his disciples entered.
Judas too, his betrayer, knew that place, for Jesus had often gone there with his disciples.
So Judas took a band of people from the chief priests and servants of the Pharisees, and came there with torches and lamps and weapons.
But Jesus, knowing all that was coming upon him, went out and said to them: Whom do you seek?
They answered and said to him: Jesus the Nazarene. Jesus said to them: I am he. Judas too, his betrayer, was standing with them.
And when he said to them, I am he, they turned back and fell to the ground.
And then he asked them again: Whom do you seek? And they said to him: Jesus the Nazarene.
Jesus said to them: I told you that I am he. If you are seeking me, let these men go, let them depart.
This was so that the word Jesus had spoken to them might be fulfilled: Of those whom you gave me, I will not lose even one.
Now Simon Peter had a sword; he drew it and struck the servant of the high priest and cut off his right ear. And the name of that servant was Malchus.
Jesus said to Peter: Put the sword into the sheath! The cup which the Father has given me, shall I not drink it?
Then the band and the captain of a thousand and the attendants of the Jews seized Jesus and bound him.
And they led him first to Annas, for he was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, who was high priest that year.
Now it was Caiaphas who had advised the Jews that it was better for one man to die for the people.
And Simon Peter followed Jesus, and so did the other disciple. Now that one disciple was known to the high priest, and he went in with Jesus into the courtyard of the high priest.
But Peter stood outside by the door. The other disciple, who was known to the high priest, went out and spoke to the woman who kept the door, and brought Peter in.
The maidservant who kept the door said to Peter: Surely you too are not one of this man's disciples? And Peter said: I am not.

The servants and the attendants of the high priests were standing there; they had kindled a charcoal fire, for it was cold, and they were warming themselves. And Peter too was with them, standing and warming himself.
Then the high priest questioned Jesus about his disciples and about his teaching.
Jesus answered him and said: I have spoken openly to the world, and I always taught in the synagogue and in the temple, where all the Jews gather, and I said nothing in secret.
Why do you ask me? Ask those who heard what I taught them. Look, these people know what I said to them."
And when he had said this, one of the attendants standing by struck Jesus on the cheek and said to him: Is this how you answer the high priest?
Jesus said to him: If I have spoken evil, testify about the evil; but if good, why do you strike me?
And Annas sent him bound to Caiaphas, the high priest.
Now Simon Peter was standing and warming himself. Those standing there said to him: Surely you too are not one of his disciples? He denied it and said: I am not.
One of the servants of the high priest, a relative of the man whose ear had been cut off, said to him: Did I not see you in the garden with him?
And then Peter denied it again. And immediately a rooster crowed.
And they brought Jesus from Caiaphas to the praetorium. And it was dawn. And they themselves did not go into the praetorium, so that they might not be defiled, but might eat the Passover.
Pilate came out to them and said to them: What accusation do you bring against this man?
They answered and said to him: If he were not an evildoer, we would not have handed him over to you.
Pilate said to them: Take him yourselves and judge him according to your law. The Jews said to him: It is not lawful for us to put anyone to death.
This was so that the word of Jesus might be fulfilled, which he spoke when he made known by what death he was going to die.
Pilate went into the praetorium again and called Jesus there and said to him: Are you the king of the Jews?
Jesus said to him: Do you say this of your own accord, or did others tell you about me?
Pilate answered him and said: Am I a Jew? Your own people and the high priests have handed you over to me. What have you done?

Jesus answered him and said: "My kingdom is not of this world. If my kingdom were of this world, my servants would have fought for me, so that I would not be handed over to the Jews. But now my kingdom is not from here in this world."

Pilate said to him: "So are you a king?" Jesus said to him: "You say that I am a king. For this I was born, and for this I was sent into the world: to bear witness to the truth. Everyone who is of the truth will hear my voice."
Pilate said to him: "What is truth?" And when he had said this, he went out again to the Jews and said to them: "I have found no guilt in him at all."
"But it is your custom that I release one person to you at this Passover. Do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews?"
They all cried out and said: "Not that man, but Barabbas!" And this Barabbas was a robber.
Then Pilate took Jesus and had him tortured.
And the soldiers wove a crown of thorns, put it on his head, and dressed him in a purple robe.
And they kept coming up to him and saying: "Hail, King of the Jews!" And they struck him on the cheek.
Pilate went outside again and said to them: "Behold, I am bringing him out to you, so that you may know that I have found no guilt in him at all."
Jesus came outside, wearing the crown of thorns and the purple garment, and Pilate said to them: "Behold, the man!"
And when the chief priests and the servants saw the man, they cried out and said: "Crucify, crucify him!" Pilate said to them: "Take him yourselves and crucify him, for I find no guilt in him."
The Jews answered him and said: "We have a law, and according to our law he must die, because he made himself the Son of God."
When Pilate heard these words, he was all the more afraid.
And he went in again and said to Jesus: "Where are you from?" But Jesus gave him no answer.
Pilate said to him: "Do you say nothing to me? Do you not know that I have authority to crucify you and I have authority to release you?"
Jesus said to him: "You would have no authority over me at all, if it had not been given to you from above. Therefore the one who handed me over to you has the greater sin."
Because of this Pilate wanted to release him, but the Jews cried out and said: "If you release this man, you are no friend of Caesar, for everyone who calls himself a king speaks against Caesar."
When Pilate heard these words, he brought Jesus outside and sat down on the judgment seat, in the place called the Stone Pavement, and in Hebrew Gabbatha.
And it was the Friday of the Passover; the hour was about the sixth. And he said to the Jews: "Behold, your king!"

But they cried out and said: "Take him away, take him away and crucify him!" Pilate said to them: "Shall I crucify your king?" The chief priests answered and said to him: "We have no king but Caesar."
Then he handed him over to them to be crucified, and they led him away.
And carrying his cross himself, he went out to the place of the Skull, which is called in Hebrew Golgotha,
where they crucified him, and with him two others, one on this side and one on that, and Jesus in the middle.
And Pilate wrote a tablet and placed it on the cross. And the inscription read thus: "Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews."
Many of the Jews read this tablet, because the place where they crucified Jesus was near the city. And the inscription was in Hebrew, in Latin, and in Greek.
The chief priests of the Jews said to Pilate: Do not write him as King of the Jews, but that he said: I am King of the Jews.
Pilate said to them: "What I have written, I have written."
Now the soldiers who crucified Jesus took his garments and divided them into four parts, a part for each soldier, and also the tunic. The tunic was seamless, woven from the top throughout.

And they said to one another: Let us not tear this, but let us cast lots over it to see whose it will be, so that the scripture might be fulfilled: They divided my garments among themselves, and over my tunic they cast lots. This is what the soldiers did.
Standing by the cross were his mother and his mother's sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene.
When Jesus saw his mother and the disciple whom he loved standing before him, he said to his mother: Woman, behold, your son!
And then he said to the disciple: Behold, your mother! From that day the disciple took her to his own home.
After this Jesus saw that everything had been accomplished; so that the scripture might be fulfilled, he said: I thirst.
A vessel full of vinegar stood there. And they filled a sponge with the vinegar, together with hyssop, and put it on a reed and brought it to his mouth.
And when Jesus had received the vinegar, he said: This scripture too has been fulfilled. And he bowed his head and gave up his spirit.

Now the Jews, because it was Friday, so that his body should not remain on the cross until the Sabbath, for that day of the Sabbath was a great one, asked Pilate that their legs might be broken and that they might be taken away.
The soldiers came and broke the legs of the first, and likewise of the other who had been crucified with him.
But when they came to Jesus and saw that he had died, they did not break his legs,
but one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and immediately blood and water came out.
And he who saw it has testified, and his testimony is true, and he knows that he is telling the truth, so that you too may believe.
This happened so that the scripture might be fulfilled: "His bone shall not be broken."
And another book says: They will look on him whom they pierced.

After this Joseph, who was from Arimathea, who was a disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Jews, asked Pilate that he might take away the body of Jesus. And Pilate gave him the order. They came and took away his body.
Nicodemus also came, he who had first come to Jesus by night, and he brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred litrai.
And they took the body of Jesus and wrapped it in linen cloths, wrappings [?], with the spices, as is the burial custom of the Jews.
In the place where he was crucified there was a garden, and in the garden a new tomb, where no one had been laid.
There they laid the body of Jesus because of the Friday of the Jews, for the tomb was nearby.
On the first day of the week Mary Magdalene came to the tomb at dawn, while it was still dark, and saw the stone taken away from the door of the tomb.
She ran and came to Simon Peter and to the other disciple, whom Jesus loved, and said to them: They have taken the Lord from the tomb, and I do not know where they have laid him.
Peter and the other disciple went out and were going to the tomb.
The two of them ran together. But the one disciple ran ahead, faster than Peter, and came first to the tomb.
And he looked down into the tomb and saw the linen cloths lying there, but he did not go inside.
Then Simon Peter also came after him and went into the tomb. He saw the linen cloths lying there,
And the face-cloth that had been on his head was not lying with the linen cloths, but was folded up by itself in one place.
Then the other disciple also went in, the one who had come to the tomb first, before Peter. And they saw and believed.
For they did not yet know the scripture, that he must rise from the dead.
The disciples went away again by themselves.
But Mary stood outside by the tomb and was weeping. And as she wept, she looked down into the tomb,
And she saw two angels clothed in white, sitting where the body of the Lord Jesus had lain, one at the head and one at the feet.
and the angels said to her: "Woman, why are you weeping?" And she said to them: "They have taken my Lord from the tomb, and I do not know where they have laid him."
When she had said this, she turned back and saw Jesus standing, and she did not know that it was Jesus.

Jesus said to her: "Woman, why are you weeping? Whom are you seeking?" She thought that he was the gardener, and she said to him: "Lord, if you have taken him away, tell me where you have laid him, so that I may carry him away."
Jesus said to her: "Mary!" She turned around and said to him in Hebrew: "Rabbi!" which means Teacher. And she ran to meet him.
Jesus said to her: "Do not touch me, for I have not yet ascended to my Father. Go to my brothers and say to them: I am ascending to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God."
Mary Magdalene came to tell his disciples that she had seen the Lord and that he had said this to her.
And when evening came on that first day of the week, and the doors were shut where the disciples were hidden for fear of the Jews, Jesus came, stood among them, and said to them: "Peace be with you!"
And when he had said this, he showed them his hands and his side. And the disciples rejoiced when they saw the Lord.
Jesus said to them again: "Peace be with you! As the Father has sent me, so I also send you."
And when he had said this, he breathed on them and said: "Receive the Holy Spirit."
"If you forgive anyone their sins, they will be forgiven them; if you retain them for anyone, they will be retained."
But Thomas, one of the Twelve, who was called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came.

The other disciples were telling him: "We have seen the Lord." But he said to them: "Unless I see in his hands the mark of the nails, and put my fingers into the place of the nails, and lay my hand on his side, I will never believe."
And after eight days the disciples were again gathered inside, and Thomas was with them too. And Jesus came in, though the doors were shut, stood among them, and said to them: "Peace be with you!"
Then he said to Thomas: "Bring your fingers here and see my hands, and lay your hand on my side, and do not be unbelieving, but believe."
Thomas answered and said to him: "My Lord and my God!"
Jesus said to him: "Because you have seen me, you believe. Blessed are those who have not seen me and have believed in me."
Jesus also did many other signs before his disciples, which are not written in this book.
But these are written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and so that you may believe and have life in his name.
After this Jesus again revealed himself to his disciples at the Sea of Tiberias. And he revealed himself in this way:
There were together Simon Peter, and Thomas who was called the Twin, and Nathanael who was from Cana of Galilee, and the sons of Zebedee, and two others of his disciples.
Simon Peter said to them: "Let us go fishing." They said to him: "We will come with you too." They went out and got into the boat. That night they caught nothing.
And as day was breaking, Jesus stood on the shore, and the disciples did not know that it was Jesus.
Jesus said to them: Children, do you have anything to eat? They answered and said to him: No.
And he said to them: Cast that net on the right side of the boat, and you will find some. So they cast it, and they could no longer haul it out because of the multitude of fish.
The disciple whom Jesus loved said to Peter: It is the Lord. And when Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he girded on his garment, for he was naked, and threw himself into the sea.
But the other disciples came by boat, for they were not far from land, only about two hundred cubits, and they were dragging the net full of fish.
And when they got out onto the land, they saw a charcoal fire laid there, with fish on it, and bread.
Jesus said to them: Bring some of those fish that you have now caught.
Simon Peter came out and dragged the net to land, full of very large fish, one hundred and fifty-three of them. And though there were so many, the net did not tear.
Jesus said to them: Come and have your meal. And none of the disciples dared any longer to ask him: Who are you? They knew that it was the Lord himself.
Jesus came and took the bread and gave it to them, and the fish likewise.
This made three times that Jesus revealed himself to his disciples after he had risen from the dead.
And when they had eaten, Jesus said to Simon Peter: Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me more than these? Peter said to him: Yes, Lord, you know that I love you. Jesus said to him: Feed my lambs.
Then he said to him a second time: Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me? Peter said to him: Yes, Lord, you know that I love you. Jesus said to him: Tend my sheep.

Jesus said to him a third time: Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me? Peter was grieved because he said to him a third time: Do you love me? Peter said to him: Lord, you know everything, and you are aware of everything, that I love you. Jesus said to him: Tend my sheep.

Amen, amen, I say to you: when you were young, you girded yourself and went wherever you wished. But when you grow old, you will stretch out your hands, and others will gird you and lead you away where you do not wish to go.
He said this to make known by what death he would glorify God. And when he had said this, he then said to him: Follow me.
Peter turned and saw the disciple whom Jesus loved, the one who at the supper had leaned on his breast and said to him: Lord, who is it that will betray you?
When Peter saw him, he said to Jesus: Lord, what do you say about this one?
Jesus said to him: If I wish him to remain until I come, what is that to you? You follow me.
And this saying spread among the brothers, that that disciple would not die. Yet Jesus did not say to him that he would not die, but: If I wish him to remain until my coming.
This is the disciple who testifies about this and who wrote this. And we know that his testimony is true.
And there are also many other things that Jesus did, which, if they were written down one by one, I do not think that this world could contain the books that would be written.
